clue.text: One cannot go straight round it

definitions.text: One cannot go straight round it

blocks.clueFragment: One cannot go straight round it
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about something that forces a detour, like an obstacle
setter's reading: going round this means curving, since the road itself is not straight

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some obstruction nobody can pass by walking directly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round it' suggests circling an obstacle; really you round it by following the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve in a road or river cannot be travelled in a straight line, so the riddle describes it.

clue.text: This Bronté derivative might be considered lucky

definitions.note: describes the thing rather than naming it

indicators.note: a derivative is made from existing material, so the letters are reworked into something new

blocks.note: taken as written, the accent ignored

explanation.surface: Something derived from a Brontë novel is said to bring good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a BIRTHSTONE is the jewel believed lucky for those born in its month.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem tied to your month of birth is traditionally thought to bring its wearer good fortune.

clue.text: Peter Pan, accepting ring, removed the stationery

indicators.note: accepting means taking something extra in, so a further letter joins the mix before shuffling
removed here means moved again, so the letters are shifted into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: The boy who never grew up takes a ring and clears away the writing materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets for writing letters on are a standard item of office and desk supplies.

clue.text: An afterthought about stopping road works

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the abbreviation for the afterthought is read backwards

blocks.note: the indefinite article
a postscript is an afterthought added to a letter
synonym: bringing to a halt

explanation.surface: Someone adds a late note about halting the roadworks.
explanation.walkthrough: PS is postscript; 'stopping' looks like part of the surface but supplies its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying a tarmac surface is exactly the kind of job that roadworks involve.

clue.text: Girl useless in school hospital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, the useless part going within the hospital

blocks.note: short for sanatorium, the sickbay at a boarding school
US is old slang abbreviation for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A girl proves no help in the school sickbay.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'san' is the sanatorium of a British boarding school; US for useless is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, so it serves as an example of a girl.

clue.text: It's not easy on the vessel for an inflexible and uncompromising person

blocks.note: something not easy is hard
a liner is a large passenger ship, placed on after the first piece

explanation.surface: Life aboard ship is tough going for a rigid, unbending character.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to a strict, unyielding policy position is called a hardliner.

clue.text: Firm restricted the number of people assembled

blocks.note: synonym: kept within limits
a company is a gathering of people

explanation.surface: A business capped how many people could gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A business whose owners' liability is restricted is a common legal form of commercial firm.

clue.text: White House up north

blocks.note: surface reading: the US president's residence in Washington
setter's reading: a home built of white snow blocks in the Arctic

explanation.surface: The presidential residence relocated somewhere in the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuit snow shelters are dome dwellings made of white compacted snow in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Refuse, not having time to dress

indicators.note: not having means going without, so the word for time is taken out

blocks.note: refuse as a noun is rubbish
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to get dressed because they are short of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, especially distinctive attire, the noun sense of dress.

clue.text: Mr Giles reportedly found dead skin said to be on the chemical

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the job of Mr Giles is used for its sound
said points to speech, so the word for dead skin is used for how it is pronounced

blocks.note: Farmer Giles is a stock figure of an English farmer
the cuticle is the dead skin at the base of a fingernail

explanation.surface: A farmer is said to have found dead skin sitting on some chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: Farmer Giles is a traditional English name for a typical farmer; say FARMER CUTICLE quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal drug is a manufactured chemical compound, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Chart movement of toothed rack

indicators.note: movement means the letters shift position into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A graph tracks how a toothed mechanical bar moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratch is an older word for a ratchet, a notched bar engaged by a pawl.

clue.text: Motorcyclist's telephone device

blocks.note: first meaning: a rider in motocross over rough ground
second meaning: a gadget that garbles a call so eavesdroppers cannot follow

explanation.surface: A biker's phone gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an off-road racing rider and a gadget that encrypts phone speech.

clue.text: Extremely high rise in prices at large supermarket?

definitions.text: Extremely high rise in prices at large supermarket?

blocks.note: surface reading: steep price increases in an economy
setter's reading: a very large store is a hypermarket, joined to the word for rising prices

explanation.surface: Shoppers notice soaring prices at a huge superstore.
explanation.definitionFit: Runaway, extreme price growth across an economy is the economists' term described here.

clue.text: Gambler intended, as one might say, to make improvement

indicators.note: as one might say means the word is taken for how it is spoken

blocks.note: one who bets, also spelt bettor
intended means meant

explanation.surface: A punter planned to better himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Betterment is the process of making something or someone better, so it is improvement.

clue.text: Shapely hedge-trimmer?

blocks.note: surface reading: a well-built, attractive person
setter's reading: one who clips shrubs into shapes

explanation.surface: An attractive gardener cutting the hedge.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of topiary clips bushes into ornamental figures and geometric forms.

clue.text: name no-good hospital endlessly included - it's leaning!

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut
included means placed inside, so the shortened hospital goes within the rest

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
a clinic is a medical centre
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a hopeless hospital and declares it is tilting.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed the clue starts lower-case and lacks its opening 'I', which supplies the first letter; the setter's first word was lost in the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclining means sloping or tilting, the participle sense of leaning.

clue.text: Lament ride round that includes Grangemouth!

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the letters of the word ride are mixed
includes means takes inside, so the shuffled word wraps the selected letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the mouth of Grange, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A mournful trip around the Scottish port of Grangemouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Grangemouth is a refinery town on the Firth of Forth; read it as Grange's mouth, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a slow mournful song, a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Fix again, retain pop version

indicators.note: a version is a reworked form, so the letters come out in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Arrange things again so a pop music version is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint is to fix or settle on, so doing so a second time is reappointing.

clue.text: Patient attendant

blocks.note: surface reading: a helper who never loses their temper
setter's reading: a noun, someone being treated, whom this person looks after

explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like an adjective praising the attendant; it is the noun for the person being cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital worker who cares for the sick is the attendant of each person under treatment.

clue.text: Troops can sort out electrical discharge

indicators.note: sort out means rearrange into order, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers are able to deal with a power surge.
explanation.definitionFit: St Elmo's fire, the glow seen on ships' masts in storms, is a luminous atmospheric discharge.

clue.text: Explosive stationery?

blocks.note: surface reading: something that blows up, like the charge in a gun round
setter's reading: a heavy drawing paper whose name happens to begin with an ammunition word

explanation.surface: Writing supplies that might go off with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick, rough drawing paper used by artists takes its name from the paper once used for gun charges.

clue.text: Not starting to be a less hairy tree!

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: less hairy means more bald

explanation.surface: Someone avoids going bald by becoming a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Visitors not having time to think

indicators.note: not having means doing without, so the letter for time is removed

blocks.note: synonym: people visiting
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Visitors are too busy to stop and reflect.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage, to guess is to suppose or reckon, as in I guess so.

clue.text: Some much as health-giving as stew

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of much, all of as, and the start of health

explanation.surface: A stew is supposedly about as nourishing as anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped meat cooked again, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Habit-forming colorant about to be included

indicators.note: included means placed inside, so the short word for about goes within the colorant

blocks.note: colouring is a common food additive
c is circa, about

explanation.surface: A food dye is about to be shown to be habit-forming.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive creates dependence, so it is habit-forming.

clue.text: Innocent one enters the body of the church

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the numeral goes inside the part of the church

blocks.note: the nave is the main central part of a church
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A guileless person walks into the main hall of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and lacking experience, synonymous with innocent.

clue.text: Timely manufacturer?

blocks.note: surface reading: punctual, arriving on schedule
setter's reading: one who makes timepieces, so dealing in time

explanation.surface: A firm that always delivers on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Horology is the study and making of clocks and watches, so its expert builds timepieces.

clue.text: Incorrect instruction?

blocks.note: surface reading: a wrong order or direction
setter's reading: in-correct, an editor's mark telling the printer not to correct, to let it stand

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Incorrect' as not to be corrected rather than wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders write this Latin mark, meaning let it stand, to cancel an earlier correction.
